Runtime-resolved via @domain_yaml — compiled once, runs against any domain shaped the same way.

Second rung of the verifier ladder: LLM parses NL problem → Sage kernel computes exact answer (Galois group, rational point, elliptic curve rank, factorization) → LLM explains. Requires --kernel-name sagemath.

Top rung of the verifier ladder (milestone B-3): LLM formalizes a prose claim → Lean 4 elaborates the statement → LLM writes tactics → Lean kernel-checks the proof. Repair loops fed Lean's actual diagnostics (≤ max_tries). Badges: machine_proved (kernel-checked) / statement_checked / unverified. Citation path (exact?) runs before proof-writing — a library hit costs zero tokens. Built on spl3/lean_bridge.py (15/15 tests green).

Capstone of the verifier ladder: ONE declarative workflow puts all three deterministic rungs (SymPy from recipe 67, SageMath from recipe 75, Lean 4 + mathlib from recipe 76) behind the same problem text via a single --param backend= flip. LLM decomposes/formalizes/narrates (probabilistic); the chosen kernel computes exact instances (SymPy/Sage) or kernel-checks statements against mathlib (Lean), returning a badge (machine_proved/statement_checked/unfaithful/unverified). enable_solver=false runs the unaided-LLM baseline for direct A/B comparison. Backed by a cross-model experiment harness (run_experiment.py) with round-trip verification across ~1,200 cells.

Demonstrates SPL's deterministic-probabilistic boundary: LLM reads a natural-language LP problem and generates PuLP solver code (probabilistic), PuLP/CBC finds the optimal solution with a proof of optimality (deterministic), ASSERT gates on solver status (formal verification), LLM interprets the result (probabilistic). Repair loop retries up to max_tries on Error/Infeasible. Default problem: bakery production planning (known optimum: bread=3, croissants=3, profit=$60). Requires: pip install pulp.

Upgrades recipe 50 (code_pipeline) by replacing the LLM-simulated test step with real pytest execution. LLM generates code AND tests independently from the spec; CALL run_pytest() executes both in a subprocess; ASSERT all_tests_passed() gates on the deterministic verdict. The repair loop feeds actual pytest tracebacks back to the LLM. Demonstrates that SPL's ASSERT is a formal correctness certificate, not a proxy for execution success. TMLR appendix: Domain #3 — Software Development.
OpenCV measures pixels deterministically and cheaply, SPL's LLM step reasons over the resulting structured report.

Extends the verifier ladder into discrete/combinatorial math: LLM reads a natural-language graph problem and writes networkx code (probabilistic), networkx computes the exact shortest-path/bipartite/cycle answer (deterministic), ASSERT gates on tool success, LLM interprets the result and restates a Final answer line, a deterministic classify_roundtrip() check confirms the LLM's stated answer matches the networkx ground truth. Repair loop retries up to max_tries on Error. Default problem: 6-warehouse shortest-path network (known optimum: A-C-B-D-E-F, distance=13). Requires: networkx (already installed).

Adds a CSP verifier class distinct from 78's LP/numeric optimization: LLM reads a natural-language zebra-style logic puzzle and writes python-constraint code (probabilistic), the CSP solver enumerates all solutions (deterministic), ASSERT gates on a Unique solution being found, LLM interprets the result and restates a Final answer line, a deterministic classify_roundtrip() check confirms the LLM's stated answer matches the solver's unique solution. Repair loop retries up to max_tries on Error/Ambiguous/NoSolution. Default problem: 3-house zebra-lite puzzle (known unique answer: the Dane drinks Coffee). Requires: pip install python-constraint.

Demonstrates a categorical (not numeric-fuzzy) verifier for physics/engineering word problems: LLM writes pint unit-aware code (probabilistic), pint executes the calculation with units attached and raises DimensionalityError on any unit mismatch (deterministic), ASSERT gates on dimensional consistency, LLM interprets the result and restates a Final answer line, a deterministic classify_roundtrip() check confirms the LLM's stated answer matches pint's computed magnitude (0.5% tolerance). Repair loop retries up to max_tries on Error. Default problem: kinematics (car accelerating from rest; known answer: 108 km/h). Requires: pip install pint.

Text-to-SQL with a row-level verifier: LLM writes a SQL SELECT from a natural-language question (probabilistic), stdlib sqlite3 executes it against a seeded in-memory database (deterministic), ASSERT gates on clean execution, a deterministic classify_roundtrip() function row-diffs the LLM's result against an independently-authored ground-truth SQL query over the same seeded data, LLM interprets the verified rows. Repair loop retries up to max_tries on SQL error. Default question: average Engineering salary (known ground truth: $97,333.33). Requires: stdlib sqlite3 only, no new pip dependency.

Upgrades recipe 79's example-based pytest verification one rung further: LLM generates an implementation AND independent Hypothesis properties from the same spec (probabilistic), pytest+Hypothesis execute the properties against hundreds of auto-generated inputs in a subprocess (deterministic), ASSERT gates on all properties passing (a genuine falsifying example is never repaired away, only broken test-harness code is), LLM interprets the verified result, a deterministic classify_roundtrip() check confirms the LLM's narration agrees with the actual pass/fail verdict. Default spec: merge two sorted lists. Requires: pip install hypothesis pytest.

Demonstrates exact closed-form arithmetic verification for compound-interest/loan-amortization word problems: LLM writes stdlib decimal code implementing the correct formula (probabilistic), Decimal arithmetic computes the exact figure with no floating-point drift (deterministic), ASSERT gates on clean execution, LLM interprets the result and restates a Final answer line, a deterministic classify_roundtrip() check confirms the LLM's stated dollar figure matches the Decimal-computed ground truth (1 cent / 0.5% tolerance). Repair loop retries up to max_tries on Error. Default problem: 5-year loan amortization (known answer: $193.33/month). Requires: stdlib decimal only, no new pip dependency.

A second, harder optimization class beyond recipe 78's linear program: LLM writes Google OR-Tools vehicle-routing code from a natural-language logistics problem (probabilistic), OR-Tools' combinatorial routing solver searches the NP-hard space and returns a feasible route with its total distance (deterministic), ASSERT gates on a feasible route being found, LLM interprets the route and restates a Final answer line, a deterministic classify_roundtrip() check confirms the LLM's stated total distance matches the solver's computed ground truth. Repair loop retries up to max_tries on Error. Default problem: 1 depot + 5 customer TSP (known optimum: 101 miles). Requires: pip install ortools.

Opens the computational-science domain: a categorical + numeric verifier for 1-D collision problems. LLM writes NumPy code reporting final-state velocities (probabilistic); run_conservation_check() independently recomputes total momentum and kinetic energy before/after from the reported values (deterministic, never trusts the code's own self-report); ASSERT gates on momentum (and, for elastic collisions, energy) being conserved within 1% tolerance. Repair loop retries up to max_tries on a conservation-law violation. LLM interprets the verified velocity and restates a Final answer line, cross-checked by classify_roundtrip() (0.5% tolerance). Default problem: elastic collision, equal masses (known answer: ball 1 stops at 0 m/s). Requires: numpy only, no new pip dependency.

Second computational-science recipe: a categorical mass-balance verifier for chemical equations, with no chemistry library dependency. LLM proposes a strict-format balanced equation with explicit integer coefficients (probabilistic); run_balance_check() parses every formula (recursive-descent parser, supports parentheses e.g. Ca(OH)2) and sums atoms x coefficient per element on each side (deterministic); ASSERT gates on exact mass balance for every element. Repair loop retries up to max_tries on a mismatched element. LLM interprets the verified equation and restates a Final answer coefficient line, cross-checked by classify_roundtrip(). Default problem: combustion of methane (known answer: 1 CH4 + 2 O2 -> 1 CO2 + 2 H2O). Requires: stdlib re only, no new pip dependency.

Third computational-science recipe: stacks two independent oracles (categorical symmetry + numeric density round-trip) in one ASSERT. LLM writes Python code reporting a crystal system, lattice parameters, Z, molar mass, and computed density (probabilistic); run_materials_check() independently verifies the claimed crystal system's own symmetry constraints (cubic: a=b=c, angles=90; hexagonal: a=b, gamma=120; etc.) and recomputes cell volume (general triclinic formula) and theoretical density from scratch via Avogadro's number (deterministic); ASSERT gates on both symmetry holding and density matching within 1%. Repair loop retries up to max_tries. LLM interprets the verified density and restates a Final answer line, cross-checked by classify_roundtrip(). Default problem: NaCl rock-salt structure (known answer: ~2.1636 g/cm^3). Requires: stdlib math only, no new pip dependency.

Opens the automated-planning domain: GENERATE plan -> CALL validator -> ASSERT valid -> WHILE repair, the two-phase pattern applied to STRIPS-style planning (LLM+P / DUPLEX generalized into a head-to-head baseline). LLM proposes a grounded JSON action plan over a fixed logistics-lite domain (truck, packages, locations; drive/load/unload actions) (probabilistic); run_plan_check() replays the plan action-by-action against the domain's STRIPS precondition/effect semantics, a minimal VAL-style validator (deterministic); ASSERT gates on every action's precondition holding AND the goal being reached. Repair loop retries up to max_tries, fed the exact failing step and reason. LLM interprets the validated plan and restates a Final answer step-count line, cross-checked by classify_roundtrip(). Default problem: deliver 2 packages to a common destination (known minimal plan: 6 steps). Requires: stdlib json only, no new pip dependency.

Opens the data-engineering domain, extending recipe 84's row-diff verifier with Great-Expectations-style data-quality gates. LLM writes SQL from a natural-language question (probabilistic); run_quality_gated_sql() checks referential integrity (every orders.customer_id exists in customers.id), requires a non-empty result, and computes the same statistic two structurally independent SQL formulations (AVG(x) vs SUM(x)/COUNT(x)) asserting they agree within 1e-6 (deterministic, independent of the LLM's query); ASSERT gates on clean execution AND all quality gates passing. Repair loop retries up to max_tries on any gate failure. classify_roundtrip() row-diffs (order-insensitive, float-tolerant) the LLM's result against an independently-authored ground-truth query; LLM interprets the verified, quality-gated answer. Default question: average Enterprise-segment order amount (known ground truth: $6,000.00). Requires: stdlib sqlite3 only, no new pip dependency.

The 'unexpected domain' demonstration: an LLM harmonizes a given soprano melody into a four-part chorale (probabilistic); check_voice_leading() deterministically checks parallel fifths/octaves between every voice pair across consecutive beats, voice crossing, adjacent-voice spacing, and large leaps (pure interval arithmetic on MIDI pitch numbers, stdlib json only -- no music21 dependency). Repair loop lets the LLM revise A/T/B only, up to max_tries; ASSERT gates on zero violations. classify_roundtrip() confirms the soprano voice still matches the original input melody note-for-note, catching the LLM 'fixing' a violation by silently altering the given melody instead. Default melody: C5 D5 E5 F5 G5 F5 E5 C5 (8 beats). Verified 2026-07-26: the checker correctly caught real parallel octaves/fifths from a model's naive parallel-motion harmonization. Requires: stdlib json only, no new pip dependency.

SYNTHETIC DEMO ONLY (not a clinical tool). Demonstrates the two-mode split as non-optional: an LLM extracts a structured drug list (name/dose/frequency) from a free-text clinical note (probabilistic); screen_regimen() normalizes names via a synthetic RxNorm-style alias table and checks every pairwise combination against a synthetic DrugBank-style severity table (deterministic). A contraindicated result is a load-bearing safety gate that halts BEFORE narration, unconditionally, drafting a clinical alert instead. A moderate result enters a bounded WHILE repair loop (LLM suggests dropping/substituting one drug, kernel re-screens). ASSERT gates on nothing severe/contraindicated remaining. classify_roundtrip() deterministically recounts drug mentions in the note against the LLM's extraction count, catching silently dropped/invented medications. Default note: sildenafil + nitroglycerin (a well-known contraindicated pair -- life-threatening hypotension). Verified end-to-end 2026-07-26 with ollama:gemma4 on both the contraindicated-halt path and the moderate-repair-loop path. Requires: stdlib json/re only, no new pip dependency.

Classic job-shop scheduling: N jobs x M machines, each job has a fixed sequence of operations. LLM extracts problem structure from natural language (probabilistic); solve_job_shop() runs OR-Tools CP-SAT constraint programming to find the provably-optimal schedule with minimum makespan (deterministic). ASSERT gates on OPTIMAL/FEASIBLE CP-SAT status. Ablation: use_solver=false lets the LLM schedule directly; verify_job_shop() back-substitutes to check no-overlap and precedence constraints. format_gantt() renders an ASCII Gantt chart. Demonstrates C5 (constraint propagation / CP-SAT) solver class. Solver class: C5. Requires: pip install ortools.

Personal investment demo: given a capital amount and a pool of stock tickers, minimize portfolio variance subject to a target annual return using Markowitz mean-variance optimization. fetch_stock_data() downloads historical prices via yfinance and computes annual returns and covariance matrix (deterministic). optimize_portfolio() runs cvxpy CLARABEL interior-point QP solver (deterministic). ASSERT gates on OPTIMAL status; repair loop relaxes the target return if infeasible. Ablation: use_solver=false lets the LLM suggest weights heuristically; verify_portfolio() checks weight sum, bounds, and non-negativity. LLM interprets weights and capital allocation in plain language. Adaptive: run monthly with fresh data for rebalancing signals. Not financial advice. Requires: pip install cvxpy yfinance.
Supply sourcing Pareto: minimize cost vs maximize fill rate across 3 suppliers (1000 units) via PuLP epsilon-constraint sweep (B1 benchmark)
Production sustainability Pareto: maximize profit vs minimize carbon footprint for 2 products via PuLP scalarization sweep (B3 benchmark)
Workforce 3-objective Pareto surface: minimize cost / maximize quality / minimize risk across 3 shifts via pymoo NSGA-II (B4 benchmark)
Robust supply chain MILP: binary build-vs-lease decision under 3 demand scenarios; two-stage stochastic — naive heuristic says BUILD but MILP finds LEASE saves $1140 (B5 benchmark)

Loan eligibility policy with 5 interconnected rules. Z3 finds SAT (qualifying profile exists) or UNSAT (contradictory rules). Hidden constraint: self-employed + income $40-49K ineligible even with 700 credit score — Z3 surfaces this; LLM misses it.

GE-style expectation suite on 500-row sales dataset. 10 expectations: not_null / between / in_set / unique. Injected: 12 negative amounts / 8 null customer_ids / 5 duplicate IDs / 3 invalid regions. LLM inspects description and misses all four issues.

DataFrameSchema on 200-row employee payroll. Lazy validation collects all violations in one pass. Injected: 6 salary=0 / 4 department=Temp / 3 null names. pandera catches all; LLM eyeballing sample rows misses edge cases.

Pure-Python backward-chaining inference on 4-rule insurance policy. alice=ELIGIBLE (deductible path / 3 levels) / bob=NOT ELIGIBLE (basic policy only) / carol=ELIGIBLE (catastrophic_event bypass / 4 levels). LLM misses carol's indirect proof path.

3 delivery zones in Maplewood (10×8 km). Zone A∩B overlap=6 km² (routing conflict) / northeast gap=4 km² (C004 and C005 unassigned). Coverage ratio=95%. Shapely computes exact geometry; LLM estimates gap as small.

SaaS pricing duopoly: 2 firms simultaneously choose High ($100) or Low ($70). LLM recommends cooperative High/High ($40K each). Nash support enumeration: (Low/Low) is the unique dominant-strategy equilibrium — Prisoner's Dilemma. PD gap=$15K/mo per firm.

Leader-follower pricing (extensive form). Leader commits first; backward induction finds SPNE=(Low, Low)=(Leader $28K / Follower $22K). LLM says price High to signal quality; BI proves follower always undercuts High → leader earns only $12K.

SaaS pricing: tune (monthly_price / annual_discount_pct / trial_days) to maximize customer LTV. Non-convex black-box simulation (churn + conversion). Optuna TPE 50 trials: LTV≈$218 vs LLM naive guess $172 (+21%). No gradient available.

Web page conversion: tune (headline_score / layout_score / cta_placement) on [0,1] with 25-trial budget. True optimum at (0.75 / 0.85 / 0.60) ≈ 20% conversion. GP+EI beats random search by ~60% relative on same budget by concentrating trials near the promising region.

Two nonlinear profit problems: (1) pricing — power-law demand curve (p*=MC/(1-1/ε)), SLSQP finds closed-form optimum; (2) logistics — quadratic revenue/cost surface, differential_evolution for global search. Fills the gap between LP (linear formula) and black-box BO (no formula): use when objective is a known nonlinear expression. LLM estimates; scipy verifies by back-substitution.
known_optimal: pricing: p*=MC/(1-1/ε); logistics: differential_evolution global optimum
